chapter: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Driving Jelly's brakeless bus into New York
summary: As the band breaks up, Thomas drives the bus into Manhattan, stopped by a cop in Central Park and stopping it against curbs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's interesting. That's easy to understand. Because we had those big old dollar bills...

Yeah, right. And I don't know who was President then, if it was Roosevelt or what -- but he changed the size of that money. And then we came to New York, and I had to drive the bus. I got to... Well, I knew how to drive. I learned how to drive a Ford and all thee cars out in Minneapolis. So I drove the bus into the New York.
What, Jelly Roll bought a bus?

Yeah. And the band was kind of breaking up then. I drove the bus, and I'm comin' through Central Park, because I'd been to New York before, and I know... Central Park used to be a two-way street, and then they finally changed it to one way. I didn't know it was one-way, and I didn't know buses wasn't allowed in New York. I just knew there was a road. And I'm driving, and a cop stopped me and said, 'Where are you going?' I knew where I was going. I was going up to 135th Street to a hotel where we could get rooms for cheap, because we had to...
Oh, you'd come through the tunnel downtown.
Yes. And I had to wait until Jelly Roll got in town. But that bus didn't have no brakes on it, boy; I

don't know how I made it. But I had sense enough to go over... If I had to stop it... I didn't drive too fast. So if I knew I had to stop... It was late at night, and I'd got over and hit the curb and let the curb get me to stop. I had enough brakes that as long as I didn't go fast, I didn't have no trouble, because I could see when the light was changing, and I'd stop on the next block. I was so glad when I got that bus up on 135th Street, I didn't know what to do. Because man, it was just a drag. You know, I had to come up, come into 110th Street, and then go up Lenox Avenue...
